title: Tight post-GST latency bounds for deterministic Byzantine agreement
open: Under eventual synchrony with n parties, t < n/3 Byzantine faults, and authenticated channels: close the gap between the t+1-round lower bound (synchronous executions are admissible) and the best post-GST upper bounds (O(t·Δ) time with quadratic communication, Lewis-Pye 2022). What are the optimal leading constants and additive terms — separating fault-dependent worst-case latency, good-case (correct-leader) latency, and voting phases within a successful view? The question is metric-sensitive: views, communication rounds, and elapsed time must be stated distinctly.
status: Synchronous lower bound of t+1 rounds is classic (Dwork–Lynch–Stockmeyer 1988 — also the source of the eventual-synchrony model with GST and Δ). Linear-in-t post-GST time is achieved: Lewis-Pye (arXiv:2201.01107, Thm 1.3) gives O(tΔ) termination after GST with O(n²) communication; SQuad (arXiv:2208.09262) treats linear worst-case fault-dependent latency as asymptotically optimal and separates consensus-within-view from view synchronisation. HotStuff (arXiv:1803.05069) established linear per-view communication and responsiveness — not a bound on faulty-leader view counts; HotStuff-2 (eprint 2023/397, Malkhi–Nayak) reduces within-view commit to two phases under responsiveness. Exact constants under matched assumptions: open, and requires fixing validity, setup, communication, and responsiveness constraints before a gap claim is meaningful.
why: Every production BFT chain's worst-case latency is governed by these terms; the asymptotic race is over and the constant race lacks a precise statement — pinning it is a real theory contribution.
key_works: Dwork–Lynch–Stockmeyer, JACM 1988 (https://groups.csail.mit.edu/tds/papers/Lynch/jacm88.pdf); Lewis-Pye, arXiv:2201.01107; SQuad, arXiv:2208.09262; Yin et al. HotStuff, arXiv:1803.05069; Malkhi–Nayak HotStuff-2, eprint 2023/397.
aliases: Byzantine agreement exact latency; post-GST round bounds
source: hand:2026-10-10:ds-core (revised 2026-10-11 after external review caught a wrong citation and a misleading status line)

title: View synchronisation cost in BFT protocols
open: Achieve provably efficient view synchronisation (getting all honest parties into the same view quickly after asynchrony) with optimal message complexity and latency, composably with any consensus core.
status: HotStuff's original synchronizer was shown attackable (lost-view attacks, 2021); follow-ups (Lewis-Pye–Spiegelman lines, "Optimally Resilient Synchronizers", 2023+) give near-optimal constructions with subtle trade-offs; the full optimal composability picture is open.
why: View sync bugs are real liveness outages in production BFT; the theory lags the deployed systems.
key_works: Lewis-Pye, Spiegelman et al. synchronizer lines (arXiv 2021-2023); HotStuff analysis critiques (arXiv:2104.01808, verify).

title: Asynchronous consensus with sublinear communication
open: Determine the communication complexity floor of asynchronous Byzantine agreement with adaptive adversaries and standard cryptography.
status: Asynchronous BA classically costs O(n²) messages; 2022-2024 lines (DAG-based, "Blazing BDLS", King–Saia-style) push toward Õ(n) expected communication with cryptographic help; exact asymptotics for adaptive adversaries remain open.
why: Bandwidth is the scaling wall for large-validator-set consensus.
key_works: King–Saia, "Byzantine agreement in polynomial expected time", 2013; DAG-Rider (Keidar et al., PODC 2021); Bullshark (SOSP 2022).

title: Accountability: identifying protocol violators in BFT
open: Characterize the maximum number of provable-byzantine parties (accountability) achievable alongside optimal resilience and latency in consensus; build BFT where every safety violation yields court-admissible proofs of who broke it.
status: "Alive-but-corrupt" and accountability lines (Civit et al. 2021+; "Accountable State Machine Replication" 2023) show trade-offs invisible to classic resilience theory; full trilateral trade-off open.
why: Bridges consensus to real-world legal recourse — fault attribution as a protocol property.
key_works: Civit et al., "Accessible Accountability" (PODC 2023, verify); Colizzo et al., accountable SMR (2023).

title: Throughput-decentralization-latency trilemma with matching bounds
open: Formalize and prove (or refute) the folk trilemma: no consensus protocol simultaneously achieves (i) ≥100k TPS, (ii) fully-participatory validator sets ≥10⁴, (iii) ≤1s WAN finality, plus accountability. Currently points exist (HotStuff-committee chains, Ethereum L1, Solana-class) but no theorem delimiting the region.
status: Partial lower bounds exist per-pair (committee changes cost; gossip diameter costs); no combined impossibility or matching construction.
why: The central engineering question of public blockchain infrastructure.
key_works: Narwhal/Bullshark (SOSP 2022); Ethereum L1 literature; Solana whitepaper lines.

title: DAG-based mempool/consensus separation: optimal encoding
open: In Narwhal-style architectures (mempool DAG + thin consensus), what is the information-theoretically optimal DAG encoding for committed transactions — can ordering be derived with O(1) bytes amortized per transaction regardless of DAG width?
status: Current systems pay per-vertex overhead; subamortized-constant encodings unexplored theoretically.
why: The next 10x in BFT throughput is encoding, not signing.
key_works: Danezis et al., SOSP 2022; DAG-Rider; Flashshark lines (verify).

title: Cross-shard atomic commit without two-phase lock madness
open: Design cross-shard transactions with one-round commit (no blocking 2PC), safety under shard failures, and liveness under asynchrony — matching the best single-shard latency within constant factors.
status: 2PC/3PC classics; Spanner-class TrueTime commits (2012); Sui/Sequencer-style owned-object bypasses; one-round cross-shard under partial synchrony remains open.
why: Sharded chains and distributed databases share this exact wall.
key_works: Corbett et al., "Spanner", OSDI 2012; Gray–Lamport consensus commit lines.

title: Causal consistency at global scale with minimal metadata
open: Causal consistency with O(1) or O(log n) metadata per operation (vs classic version vectors O(n)), supporting garbage collection and partition tolerance, in production deployments.
status: COPS (2011), Eiger; recent compact-vector-clock and hash-chain lines compress metadata; the lower bound for partition-tolerant causal consistency metadata is not matched.
key_works: Lloyd et al., "Don't Settle for Eventual", SOSP 2011; vector clock compression literature.

title: quantifying the consistency-latency frontier
open: A tight formal theory of the latency-consistency trade-off under partitions (PACELC) — for each consistency level, the provable latency floor in normal operation.
status: Trade-off folklore (Abadi 2012); TACT/Probabilistically-Bounded staleness quantify windows; a general theorem is missing.
key_works: Abadi, "Consistency Tradeoffs in Modern Distributed Database Design", IEEE ICDE 2012; Bailis et al., PBS (VLDB 2012).

title: CRDT expressiveness frontier
open: Characterize the largest class of data types admitting conflict-free replicated implementations (strong eventual consistency) — is there a precise semantic criterion separating CRDT-expressible from non-expressible types (e.g., ordered sets: add-wins works, but which richer types resist)?
status: State-based/function-based CRDT theory (Shapiro et al. 2011); op-based CRDTs with causality (2017+); the expressiveness boundary remains folklore.
key_works: Shapiro et al., "Conflict-free replicated data types", 2011; Kleppmann, "Local-first software", Onward! 2019.

title: Byzantine storage capacity with dynamic faults
open: The exact capacity region of Byzantine fault-tolerant storage (erasure-coded) under adaptive adversaries with repairs — when do regenerating codes achieve the MBR/MSB points with byzantine nodes (BBR codes) at all repair bandwidths?
status: Byzantine regenerating codes (Rawat et al. lines) settle points; full region + repair-bandwidth trade-off open.
key_works: Dimakis et al., "Network coding for distributed storage", TOIT 2011; Rawat et al., BBR codes (INFOCOM 2013+).

title: Information dispersal with verifiable recovery
open: Efficient-verifiable secret/information dispersal where any quorum can verify reconstruction correctness without trusting the combiner, with O(1)-size verification objects.
status: VID lines (Henderson et al. 2022+, used in distributed validator tech); constant-size proofs open.
key_works: "Blazing the trail to Vid" lines (2022-2024, verify).

title: Optimal clock synchronization under Byzantine faults
open: Tight bounds for internal clock synchronization with Byzantine faults: the achievable skew as a function of network delay uncertainty and fault fraction — closing the gap between the Lundelius–Lynch (n/(n-f)) upper bounds and constructions.
status: Classic results (1984) with recent improvements under weaker assumptions; exact region open.

title: Network-agnostic consensus: the price of uncertainty
open: Characterize the exact overhead (messages, rounds, thresholds) of protocols correct under both synchronous and asynchronous instantiations (network-agnostic), beyond the first constructions — is the price of agnosticism Θ(1) or unbounded?
status: Blum–Dolev lines; "network-agnostic MPC" (2020+) shows surprising thresholds; consensus-side picture forming 2022-2026.

title: The accountable, decentralized, high-throughput settlement layer
open: Build: ≥100k TPS, ≥10⁴ validators, ≤1s finality, slashing-with-legal-force accountability (see trilemma above) — no system claims all four; no theorem forbids it.

title: Geo-distributed databases with exactly-once everything
open: A planetary-scale database with exactly-once semantics for all operations (reads, writes, subscriptions), serializable where requested, causal everywhere else, surviving regional loss with zero lost acknowledged writes — with honest, provable tail-latency bounds.
status: Spanner-class systems approximate pieces; the full envelope unbuilt.
